title: Dyson Sphere: Desktop Factory 1.0 Is Out With Cloud Saves and Tower Defense
excerpt: Dyson Sphere: Desktop Factory 1.0 is live on Steam with drone logistics, tower defense, cloud saves and a 7-day launch discount. Demo saves won't carry over.
content:
Most of us have left a tiny game running in the corner of the screen while homework or a spreadsheet waited. It hummed along quietly, and you peeked at it between tasks. Dyson Sphere: Desktop Factory is built for that exact habit, and its full 1.0 version went live on Steam on Tuesday, October 27, 2026.

The developer, XRT, announced the launch in a Steam post. It follows a demo phase that the developer says shaped the finished game.

“After refinement, adjustments and numerous feedback iterations from the demo phase, the complete 1.0 version is here!” – Dyson Sphere: Desktop Factory on Steam

Your Demo Save Won’t Make the Trip

Let’s start with the part that matters most if you tried the demo. Demo saves are not compatible with the full release. You will be starting a fresh factory.

There is a small consolation. Cloud save support has been added for 1.0. The developer also says you can turn on local save replacement manually in the settings menu.

Drones, Defenses and a Fully Unlocked Tech Tree

The 1.0 build includes complete automated production lines, drone logistics and tower defense systems. So your factory isn’t only about moving items from one belt to the next. You can send drones to haul things and set up defenses too.

Every building, recipe, research item and tech perk is unlocked in this version. That means nothing is locked behind a demo wall anymore. You can poke around the whole tree from the start.

The developer also lists several smaller changes:

  • Rebalanced gameplay values based on feedback
  • Numerous bug fixes
  • Improved multi-language support
  • Wallpaper mode and hidden view

Steam tags the game as Casual, Simulation and Strategy. It is Windows only.

A Factory You Can Hide While You Work

The wallpaper mode and hidden view are the unusual features here. The developer says the game has very low resource usage. If you run out of things to do, you can hide the view and get back to studying or working.

You can also play other games while it runs.

“If you find yourself with nothing to do in-game, hide the view to study or work. You can also play other games at the same time – no need to idly wait.” – Dyson Sphere: Desktop Factory on Steam

That’s a nice fit for the genre. Factory games are famous for eating whole evenings. This one is designed to sit quietly in the background instead.

Price and Launch Discount

A limited-time launch discount is active for seven days. At the time of writing, Steam lists the game at $6.79, down 15% from $7.99. That sale price won’t last past the discount window, so check the store page before you buy.

Where to Send Bug Reports

The developer asks players to report crashes, bugs or other problems in the Steam community discussions. There is also a QQ group for feedback. The developer promises to keep track of reports and fix them.

Suggestions and criticism are welcome too. In the developer’s words, they will “try my best to make adjustments.”

The post ends with a thank-you to everyone who played the demo and sent in testing notes and suggestions. According to the developer, the game took shape thanks to those players. If you were one of them, your old factory is gone, but your feedback is in the finished game.

The full game is on Steam now: https://store.steampowered.com/app/4864900
